claims.text: Setting the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
On the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service, the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable specifies the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API.
When PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is unset on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes are not registered.
The DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should point at the same host that serves PULUMI_API_DOMAIN in a self-hosted Pulumi Cloud deployment.
A separate domain for PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is not required: PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN can be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud.

The Pulumi state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the domain in the Terraform/OpenTofu configuration, `terraform login`/`tofu login` commands, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name.
A Pulumi docs page exists at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ describing Pulumi Cloud as a Terraform/OpenTofu state backend.
The Terraform/OpenTofu credential environment variable name takes the form TF_TOKEN_* derived from the domain, so the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN value is used in that variable name.
